AGED BOARD (session 6b, Part I.5). The verdict run's six edits were all on apps the same loop had generated minutes earlier, from templates it had just read — the friendliest possible case for editing, and D130 records that as an open residual. This board is from the 6a.5 era: it has been sitting at revision 3 for weeks and nothing in this session's context produced it. The point of the request is not the feature; it is whether the mechanism holds when the app is a stranger.

CONFOUND, stated before the run rather than after it: this session added a `leaderboard` TEMPLATE hours ago, and the bot can read it. So the earlier framing — that no template resembles this board — is false as of today. That does not spoil the observation but it changes what the observation is. Regenerating is now the EASY path: a close template is sitting in the skill, and this board is a stranger the loop would have to read first. An edit under those conditions is a choice against the cheaper option, and a regeneration is no longer evidence that the loop cannot edit — only that it had somewhere better to start.

Phrasing is IMPERATIVE and names the group. Both were decided by the verdict run rather than chosen here: interrogative phrasing produced a byte-identical no-op against the same witness and target, and an app named without its group was published to a same-named board in a different group.
request: In the Surface seed group's chess leaderboard, add each player's current streak of wins to their row.
behaviour: Each player's row shows how many games they have won in a row, counted from the game log — so a reader can tell a player on a three-win run from one who has three wins scattered among losses.
